description: StudyAI enrichment golden set v2: 40 authored base cases + noisy + all-covered-control variants. Shared retrieval corpus, per-concept status labels (gap/partial/covered/off_scope), aliases for matching.

statuses.gap: material and missing from note: should be reported
statuses.partial: shallow mention in note: reporting acceptable, not required
statuses.covered: already in note (evidence substring given, case-insensitive): must NOT be reported
statuses.off_scope: adjacent but not needed: must NOT be reported

stage_metrics: retrieval recall@k over expected_retrieval_targets vs the whole corpus
candidate recall over concepts[].topic/aliases (and fragment rate via fragment_tokens)
final gap precision/recall/F1 (partial ignored) + false-alarm rate on must_not_flag and zero-gap cases

ref_001_01.text: Each comparison halves the search range, so binary search takes O(log n) comparisons in the worst case. With n = 10^6 elements, at most about 20 comparisons are needed.
ref_001_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_001_02.text: Computing the midpoint as (lo + hi) / 2 can overflow fixed-width integers; lo + (hi - lo) / 2 avoids this. Loop invariants must be chosen carefully to avoid infinite loops and off-by-one errors.
ref_001_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_001_03.text: Binary search is only valid when the input is sorted by the comparison used in the search. On unsorted data the discard step can throw away the target.
ref_001_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_001_04.text: Interpolation search estimates the target position from key values and can reach O(log log n) on uniformly distributed data but degrades to O(n) on skewed data.
ref_001_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_002_01.text: Electrical power dissipated in a resistor is P = VI = I²R = V²/R. This energy appears as heat, known as Joule heating.
ref_002_01.subject: Physics

ref_002_02.text: Ohmic materials have a linear I–V curve with constant resistance. Diodes, filament bulbs and thermistors are non-ohmic: resistance changes with voltage or temperature.
ref_002_02.subject: Physics

ref_002_03.text: Resistance depends on geometry: R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length and A is cross-sectional area.
ref_002_03.subject: Physics

ref_002_04.text: Resistance is the opposition to current flow, measured in ohms (Ω), with 1 Ω = 1 V/A.
ref_002_04.subject: Physics

ref_002_05.text: Kirchhoff's current law states currents entering a junction sum to zero; the voltage law states voltage changes around any closed loop sum to zero.
ref_002_05.subject: Physics

ref_003_01.text: The cell cycle is controlled by checkpoints at G1/S, G2/M and the spindle assembly checkpoint. Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) paired with cyclins drive progression through each stage.
ref_003_01.subject: Biology

ref_003_02.text: Cytokinesis physically divides the cytoplasm after mitosis. Animal cells form a contractile cleavage furrow, whereas plant cells build a cell plate.
ref_003_02.subject: Biology

ref_003_03.text: Mitosis proceeds through prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase; chromosomes condense, align, separate and decondense in turn.
ref_003_03.subject: Biology

ref_003_04.text: Meiosis involves two successive divisions and produces four genetically distinct haploid gametes through crossing over and independent assortment.
ref_003_04.subject: Biology

ref_004_01.text: The production possibilities frontier shows the maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with fixed resources. Its slope measures the opportunity cost of one good in terms of the other.
ref_004_01.subject: Economics

ref_004_02.text: Sunk costs are past expenditures that cannot be recovered and should be ignored in forward-looking decisions; only marginal costs and benefits matter.
ref_004_02.subject: Economics

ref_004_03.text: A producer has a comparative advantage in a good if its opportunity cost of producing it is lower than another producer's, which is the basis for gains from trade.
ref_004_03.subject: Economics

ref_004_04.text: Scarcity means wants exceed the resources available to satisfy them, forcing choices among alternatives.
ref_004_04.subject: Economics

ref_005_01.text: Flow control prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver. The receiver advertises a window size, and the sender limits unacknowledged data to that window.
ref_005_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_005_02.text: Congestion control adapts the sending rate to network capacity. Slow start grows the congestion window exponentially until a threshold, then additive increase/multiplicative decrease (AIMD) takes over.
ref_005_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_005_03.text: Connections close with FIN and ACK exchanges in each direction; the side that closes first enters TIME_WAIT to absorb delayed segments.
ref_005_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_005_04.text: The three-way handshake synchronises initial sequence numbers: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.
ref_005_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_005_05.text: UDP is connectionless and offers no delivery, ordering or congestion guarantees, making it suitable for DNS and real-time media.
ref_005_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_006_01.text: Third normal form removes transitive dependencies: non-key attributes must depend only on the key, not on other non-key attributes.
ref_006_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_006_02.text: BCNF strengthens 3NF by requiring every determinant to be a candidate key. Some schemas in 3NF violate BCNF when overlapping candidate keys exist.
ref_006_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_006_03.text: Denormalization deliberately reintroduces redundancy to speed up read-heavy queries, at the cost of extra storage and update anomalies.
ref_006_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_006_04.text: First normal form (1NF) requires each column to hold atomic values and each row to be unique.
ref_006_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_006_05.text: Second normal form (2NF) requires 1NF and that every non-key attribute depends on the whole candidate key, not just part of it. This only matters for composite keys.
ref_006_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_01.text: If the learning rate is too large, updates overshoot and the loss can diverge; if it is too small, convergence is very slow. Schedules such as step decay or cosine annealing reduce the rate over training.
ref_007_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_02.text: Batch gradient descent uses the full dataset per update; stochastic gradient descent uses one sample and mini-batch uses a small subset. Mini-batches balance noise, speed and hardware efficiency.
ref_007_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_03.text: Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying average of past gradients, which smooths oscillations across ravines and speeds progress along consistent directions.
ref_007_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_04.text: Adaptive methods such as Adagrad, RMSProp and Adam scale each parameter's step size using running statistics of its gradients.
ref_007_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_05.text: The gradient of the loss points toward steepest ascent, so parameters are updated by subtracting the gradient scaled by the learning rate.
ref_007_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_007_06.text: Newton's method uses second-order curvature (the Hessian) to take steps, converging quickly near a minimum but costing O(d²) memory and O(d³) time per step.
ref_007_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_01.text: Switching between threads of the same process is cheaper than switching processes because the address space, and often TLB contents, need not change.
ref_008_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_02.text: Threads sharing memory can suffer race conditions when unsynchronized accesses interleave. Mutexes, semaphores and atomic operations protect critical sections.
ref_008_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_03.text: Separate processes communicate through IPC mechanisms such as pipes, sockets, message queues and shared memory, since they do not share address spaces by default.
ref_008_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_04.text: Each process has a private virtual address space, so one process cannot directly read or write another's memory.
ref_008_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_05.text: Each thread has its own stack and register state so it can run its own call chain independently.
ref_008_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_008_06.text: Green threads are scheduled by a language runtime rather than the OS kernel, allowing very cheap creation but complicating blocking system calls.
ref_008_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_009_01.text: A matrix is diagonalizable if it has n linearly independent eigenvectors; then A = PDP⁻¹ with D diagonal, which makes computing powers of A easy.
ref_009_01.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_009_02.text: Algebraic multiplicity is the number of times λ appears as a root of the characteristic polynomial; geometric multiplicity is the dimension of its eigenspace, and it never exceeds the algebraic multiplicity.
ref_009_02.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_009_03.text: Real symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors, so they can be orthogonally diagonalized as A = QΛQᵀ.
ref_009_03.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_009_04.text: The characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) has degree n, so an n×n matrix has at most n distinct eigenvalues.
ref_009_04.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_010_01.text: For launch speed v and angle θ on level ground, range R = v² sin(2θ)/g and maximum height H = v² sin²θ / (2g). Range is maximal at θ = 45°.
ref_010_01.subject: Physics

ref_010_02.text: With air resistance the trajectory is no longer a parabola: drag reduces range and makes the descent steeper than the ascent.
ref_010_02.subject: Physics

ref_010_03.text: Time of flight on level ground is T = 2 v sinθ / g, found by setting the vertical displacement to zero.
ref_010_03.subject: Physics

ref_010_04.text: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent because gravity acts only vertically, so ax = 0 and ay = −g.
ref_010_04.subject: Physics

ref_010_05.text: Uniform circular motion requires a centripetal acceleration v²/r directed toward the centre.
ref_010_05.subject: Physics

ref_011_01.text: Antibiotic use creates selection pressure: resistant bacteria survive and reproduce while susceptible ones die, so resistance alleles rapidly increase in frequency.
ref_011_01.subject: Biology

ref_011_02.text: Genetic drift is random change in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations. Founder effects and population bottlenecks are common causes.
ref_011_02.subject: Biology

ref_011_03.text: In evolutionary biology, fitness is relative reproductive success, not strength or health: the number of viable offspring an individual contributes to the next generation compared with others.
ref_011_03.subject: Biology

ref_011_04.text: Selection can only act on variation that is heritable; acquired traits that are not encoded in the genome are not passed on.
ref_011_04.subject: Biology

ref_011_05.text: Sexual selection favours traits that increase mating success, such as peacock tails, even when they reduce survival.
ref_011_05.subject: Biology

ref_012_01.text: The acid dissociation constant Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA] quantifies acid strength; pKa = −log Ka, and a smaller pKa means a stronger acid.
ref_012_01.subject: Chemistry

ref_012_02.text: A buffer contains a weak acid and its conjugate base and resists pH change. The Henderson–Hasselbalch equation gives pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]).
ref_012_02.subject: Chemistry

ref_012_03.text: In Brønsted–Lowry theory an acid donates a proton and forms its conjugate base; the stronger the acid, the weaker its conjugate base.
ref_012_03.subject: Chemistry

ref_012_04.text: Weak acids establish an equilibrium HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻ lying mostly to the left.
ref_012_04.subject: Chemistry

ref_012_05.text: A change of one pH unit corresponds to a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration.
ref_012_05.subject: Chemistry

ref_012_06.text: A titration curve plots pH against added titrant volume; the equivalence point is where moles of acid equal moles of base.
ref_012_06.subject: Chemistry

ref_013_01.text: The real interest rate is approximately the nominal rate minus expected inflation (the Fisher equation), so lenders lose purchasing power when inflation exceeds the nominal rate.
ref_013_01.subject: Economics

ref_013_02.text: Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand outpaces supply; cost-push inflation arises when higher input costs shift aggregate supply leftward.
ref_013_02.subject: Economics

ref_013_03.text: Central banks typically raise policy interest rates to cool demand and bring inflation back toward target, at the risk of slowing growth and raising unemployment.
ref_013_03.subject: Economics

ref_013_04.text: The CPI tracks the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by a typical household.
ref_013_04.subject: Economics

ref_013_05.text: Hyperinflation is extremely rapid inflation, often defined as above 50% per month, typically associated with collapsing confidence in a currency.
ref_013_05.subject: Economics

ref_014_01.text: Deep recursion can exhaust the call stack and raise a stack overflow; in many languages the default limit is only a few thousand frames.
ref_014_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_014_02.text: A tail call is a recursive call in the final position. Languages with tail-call optimization reuse the current frame, giving O(1) stack space; Python and Java do not.
ref_014_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_014_03.text: Naive recursion for Fibonacci recomputes subproblems and takes exponential time; memoization caches results to reduce it to O(n).
ref_014_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_014_04.text: Every recursive definition needs a base case that is reached after finitely many calls, or the recursion never terminates.
ref_014_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_014_05.text: A stack frame stores parameters, local variables and the return address for one call; frames are popped as calls return.
ref_014_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_014_06.text: Mutual recursion occurs when two or more functions call each other in a cycle, as in a pair of is_even and is_odd definitions.
ref_014_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_015_01.text: Kinetic energy is ½mv² and gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface is mgh. In a frictionless fall, potential energy converts into kinetic energy with their sum unchanged.
ref_015_01.subject: Physics

ref_015_02.text: Friction and drag are non-conservative: they convert mechanical energy into thermal energy, so mechanical energy alone is not conserved although total energy is.
ref_015_02.subject: Physics

ref_015_03.text: The work–energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy, W_net = ΔKE.
ref_015_03.subject: Physics

ref_015_04.text: In elastic collisions kinetic energy is conserved; in inelastic collisions some is lost to deformation and heat, though momentum is conserved in both.
ref_015_04.subject: Physics

ref_015_05.text: An isolated system exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings.
ref_015_05.subject: Physics

ref_015_06.text: Special relativity relates rest energy to mass by E = mc², showing that mass itself can be converted to other forms of energy.
ref_015_06.subject: Physics

ref_016_01.text: The core stack operations are push (add to top), pop (remove and return the top) and peek (read the top without removing it); all run in O(1) time.
ref_016_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_016_02.text: A stack can be built on a dynamic array, with amortized O(1) push, or on a singly linked list with O(1) worst-case push and pop, at the cost of pointer overhead.
ref_016_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_016_03.text: Stacks underlie function call management, expression evaluation and parsing, balanced-parentheses checks, backtracking and undo features.
ref_016_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_016_04.text: Popping from an empty stack is an underflow error; pushing onto a full fixed-capacity stack is an overflow.
ref_016_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_016_05.text: LIFO order means the most recently added element is the first one removed.
ref_016_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_016_06.text: A queue is first-in, first-out: elements are added at the rear and removed from the front.
ref_016_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_017_01.text: Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds and guanine pairs with cytosine through three, so the strands are complementary and A = T, G = C in amounts.
ref_017_01.subject: Biology

ref_017_02.text: The helix has a wider major groove and a narrower minor groove; proteins such as transcription factors read base sequences mainly through the major groove.
ref_017_02.subject: Biology

ref_017_03.text: In eukaryotes, DNA wraps around histone octamers to form nucleosomes, which fold into chromatin and further into chromosomes.
ref_017_03.subject: Biology

ref_017_04.text: The two strands run in opposite directions, one 5'→3' and the other 3'→5'.
ref_017_04.subject: Biology

ref_017_05.text: RNA is usually single-stranded, uses ribose sugar and contains uracil instead of thymine.
ref_017_05.subject: Biology

ref_018_01.text: Bayes' theorem reverses a conditional: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B). It updates a prior belief to a posterior using the likelihood of new evidence.
ref_018_01.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_018_02.text: Events A and B are independent if P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B), equivalently P(A|B) = P(A). Independence is not the same as being mutually exclusive.
ref_018_02.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_018_03.text: If B₁,…,Bₙ partition the sample space, then P(A) = Σ P(A|Bᵢ)P(Bᵢ), which is often the denominator in Bayes' theorem.
ref_018_03.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_018_04.text: Conditioning restricts the sample space to B and renormalizes probabilities by P(B).
ref_018_04.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_018_05.text: In a Markov chain the next state depends only on the current state, not on the earlier history.
ref_018_05.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_019_01.text: Atomic radius decreases across a period because increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer, and increases down a group as new shells are added.
ref_019_01.subject: Chemistry

ref_019_02.text: First ionization energy generally increases across a period and decreases down a group, with dips at group 13 and group 16 due to subshell effects.
ref_019_02.subject: Chemistry

ref_019_03.text: Electronegativity measures an atom's tendency to attract bonding electrons; it rises across a period and falls down a group, with fluorine the highest on the Pauling scale.
ref_019_03.subject: Chemistry

ref_019_04.text: Effective nuclear charge Zeff is the net attraction felt by a valence electron after inner-shell shielding; it explains most periodic trends.
ref_019_04.subject: Chemistry

ref_019_05.text: Valence electrons are those in the outermost shell and determine bonding behaviour.
ref_019_05.subject: Chemistry

ref_019_06.text: Transition metals fill d subshells, often show multiple oxidation states, and form coloured compounds.
ref_019_06.subject: Chemistry

ref_020_01.text: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table and fills unmatched right-side columns with NULL; RIGHT JOIN is symmetric, and FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both.
ref_020_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_020_02.text: A CROSS JOIN returns the Cartesian product of two tables. A self-join joins a table to itself using aliases, useful for hierarchies such as employee–manager.
ref_020_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_020_03.text: Query planners choose among nested-loop, hash and merge joins. Indexes on join columns often turn full scans into fast lookups.
ref_020_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_020_04.text: INNER JOIN outputs a row only when the join predicate is true for a pair of rows.
ref_020_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_020_05.text: A subquery is a SELECT nested inside another statement; correlated subqueries reference columns of the outer query.
ref_020_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_01.text: A kernel k(x, y) = φ(x)·φ(y) lets an SVM work in the feature space defined by φ using only pairwise evaluations of k.
ref_021_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_02.text: Common kernels include the linear kernel, the polynomial kernel (x·y + c)^d and the RBF (Gaussian) kernel exp(−γ‖x−y‖²). The RBF kernel corresponds to an infinite-dimensional feature space.
ref_021_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_03.text: A function is a valid kernel if its Gram matrix is symmetric positive semi-definite for every finite set of points (Mercer's condition).
ref_021_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_04.text: Soft-margin SVMs allow some misclassification through slack variables; the parameter C trades margin width against training errors.
ref_021_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_05.text: The operating system kernel is the core program that manages CPU scheduling, memory, and device drivers, and runs in privileged mode.
ref_021_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_021_06.text: In image processing, a convolution kernel is a small matrix slid over an image to blur, sharpen or detect edges.
ref_021_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_022_01.text: Covalent bonds share electron pairs between atoms, typically nonmetals; ionic bonds arise from electrostatic attraction between cations and anions after electron transfer.
ref_022_01.subject: Chemistry

ref_022_02.text: A bond is polar when the two atoms differ in electronegativity, producing a partial negative charge on the more electronegative atom and a dipole moment.
ref_022_02.subject: Chemistry

ref_022_03.text: Higher bond order means shorter, stronger bonds: a C≡C bond is shorter and has higher bond enthalpy than C=C or C–C.
ref_022_03.subject: Chemistry

ref_022_04.text: A government bond is a debt security: the investor lends money to the issuer and receives periodic coupon payments plus principal at maturity.
ref_022_04.subject: Chemistry

ref_023_01.text: A normal distribution N(μ, σ²) is completely specified by its mean μ and standard deviation σ.
ref_023_01.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_023_02.text: For a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two and 99.7% within three.
ref_023_02.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_023_03.text: Standardizing with z = (x − μ)/σ maps any normal variable to the standard normal N(0,1), letting probabilities be looked up in one table.
ref_023_03.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_023_04.text: The central limit theorem states that sample means of independent, identically distributed variables with finite variance approach a normal distribution as sample size grows.
ref_023_04.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_023_05.text: A normal vector to a surface at a point is perpendicular to the tangent plane at that point.
ref_023_05.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_023_06.text: Normal modes are patterns of motion in which all parts of a system oscillate at the same frequency.
ref_023_06.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_024_01.text: The page table is indexed by virtual page number and yields the physical frame number for that page.
ref_024_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_02.text: A page fault is handled by finding a free frame and reading the page from disk. The OS then updates the page table entry, whose dirty bit records whether the page must be written back on eviction.
ref_024_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_03.text: Besides LRU, common policies are FIFO, which can exhibit Belady's anomaly, and the clock algorithm, an inexpensive approximation of LRU using a reference bit.
ref_024_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_04.text: A two-level page table splits the virtual page number so that unused regions of the address space need no second-level tables, saving memory.
ref_024_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_05.text: The translation lookaside buffer (TLB) caches recent virtual-to-physical translations so most memory accesses avoid a page-table walk. A TLB miss triggers a page-table walk, and the TLB is typically flushed or tagged on context switch.
ref_024_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_06.text: Thrashing occurs when processes lack enough frames for their working sets, so the system spends most of its time servicing page faults rather than doing useful work.
ref_024_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_07.text: With demand paging pages are loaded only on first access. Copy-on-write lets fork share pages between parent and child until one writes, when the page is copied.
ref_024_07.subject: Computer Science

ref_024_08.text: Segmentation divides the address space into variable-length logical segments such as code, heap and stack, each with a base and limit.
ref_024_08.subject: Computer Science

ref_025_01.text: Passive transport needs no cellular energy because it is driven by the concentration or electrochemical gradient.
ref_025_01.subject: Biology

ref_025_02.text: Active transport uses ATP or an ion gradient to move solutes against their gradient via pumps or coupled transporters.
ref_025_02.subject: Biology

ref_025_03.text: Channel proteins form gated pores for ions, while carrier proteins change shape to shuttle specific molecules such as glucose.
ref_025_03.subject: Biology

ref_025_04.text: The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in per ATP hydrolysed, maintaining the resting membrane potential and driving secondary transport.
ref_025_04.subject: Biology

ref_025_05.text: In a hypotonic solution cells gain water and may lyse; in a hypertonic solution they lose water and shrink (crenation, or plasmolysis in plant cells); isotonic solutions cause no net movement.
ref_025_05.subject: Biology

ref_025_06.text: Secondary active transport uses the gradient of one ion, established by primary pumps, to drive another molecule across the membrane, either in the same direction (symport) or the opposite (antiport).
ref_025_06.subject: Biology

ref_025_07.text: Large molecules and particles cross the membrane in vesicles: endocytosis (including phagocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis) brings material in, and exocytosis releases it.
ref_025_07.subject: Biology

ref_025_08.text: Membrane fluidity depends on temperature, fatty-acid saturation and cholesterol, which buffers fluidity: it restrains movement when warm and prevents tight packing when cold.
ref_025_08.subject: Biology

ref_025_09.text: Plant, fungal and bacterial cells have a rigid cell wall outside the plasma membrane that provides mechanical support.
ref_025_09.subject: Biology

ref_026_01.text: A held-out test set gives an unbiased estimate of generalization only if it is never used for fitting or model selection.
ref_026_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_02.text: Accuracy is (TP + TN) divided by the total number of examples.
ref_026_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_03.text: An overfit model has low training error but high test error because it memorises idiosyncrasies of the training set.
ref_026_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_04.text: In k-fold cross-validation the data is divided into k folds; each fold is used once for validation while the remaining k − 1 train the model. Stratified folds preserve class proportions.
ref_026_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_05.text: Precision is TP/(TP+FP) and recall is TP/(TP+FN). The F1 score is their harmonic mean and is more informative than accuracy when classes are imbalanced.
ref_026_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_06.text: With 99% negatives, a classifier that always predicts negative scores 99% accuracy while detecting nothing, the accuracy paradox. Class weights and resampling help.
ref_026_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_07.text: The ROC curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate across thresholds; the area under it (AUC) measures ranking quality independent of any single threshold.
ref_026_07.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_08.text: Data leakage occurs when information from the test set influences training, for example by fitting a scaler on all the data before splitting, producing overly optimistic scores.
ref_026_08.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_09.text: The bias–variance tradeoff describes the tension between underfitting (high bias) and overfitting (high variance); expected error decomposes into bias², variance and irreducible noise.
ref_026_09.subject: Computer Science

ref_026_10.text: Reinforcement learning trains an agent to maximise cumulative reward through interaction with an environment.
ref_026_10.subject: Computer Science

ref_027_01.text: Hooke's law F = −kx gives a linear restoring force, which is why springs produce SHM.
ref_027_01.subject: Physics

ref_027_02.text: In ideal SHM the period depends only on the mass and spring constant, not on how far the mass is displaced.
ref_027_02.subject: Physics

ref_027_03.text: The differential equation m x'' = −k x has sinusoidal solutions with amplitude A and phase φ set by initial conditions.
ref_027_03.subject: Physics

ref_027_04.text: For a simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g) for small angles, using sin θ ≈ θ; at larger amplitudes the period increases slightly.
ref_027_04.subject: Physics

ref_027_05.text: In SHM the total mechanical energy E = ½kA² is constant, oscillating between kinetic energy (maximal at equilibrium) and potential energy (maximal at the turning points).
ref_027_05.subject: Physics

ref_027_06.text: With damping, amplitude decays over time. Underdamped systems oscillate with shrinking amplitude, critically damped systems return fastest without oscillating, and overdamped systems return slowly.
ref_027_06.subject: Physics

ref_027_07.text: A periodically driven oscillator responds with maximum amplitude near its natural frequency, called resonance; damping limits and broadens the resonance peak.
ref_027_07.subject: Physics

ref_027_08.text: SHM is the projection of uniform circular motion onto a diameter: a point moving at angular speed ω around a circle of radius A has a projection that oscillates as A cos(ωt + φ).
ref_027_08.subject: Physics

ref_027_09.text: Superposed waves add: constructive interference occurs when crests align, destructive when a crest meets a trough.
ref_027_09.subject: Physics

ref_028_01.text: In the array layout, the children of index i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2, so no pointers are needed.
ref_028_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_02.text: In a min-heap the smallest element is always at the root; siblings have no ordering constraint.
ref_028_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_03.text: Union-find (disjoint-set union) represents each set as a tree; find returns the root representative and union links two roots.
ref_028_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_04.text: In a trie each edge is labelled with a character and the path from the root spells a prefix, so words with common prefixes share nodes.
ref_028_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_05.text: Insert appends at the end and sifts up; extract-min swaps the root with the last element and sifts down. Both take O(log n), while building a heap from n elements with bottom-up heapify takes O(n).
ref_028_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_06.text: Heaps implement priority queues and power heapsort (O(n log n) time, in place), top-k selection, event simulation and Dijkstra's algorithm.
ref_028_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_07.text: Union by rank and path compression together make union-find operations run in amortized O(α(n)) time, where α is the inverse Ackermann function, effectively constant.
ref_028_07.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_08.text: Trie lookup, insert and prefix search take O(L) time for a key of length L regardless of the number of keys, but memory can be large; radix trees compress single-child chains.
ref_028_08.subject: Computer Science

ref_028_09.text: A segment tree answers range queries such as sum or minimum over an array in O(log n) and supports point updates.
ref_028_09.subject: Computer Science

ref_029_01.text: The light reactions produce ATP and NADPH, which the Calvin cycle uses to fix CO₂ into G3P.
ref_029_01.subject: Biology

ref_029_02.text: Cellular respiration oxidises glucose in stages: glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation.
ref_029_02.subject: Biology

ref_029_03.text: Both organelles pump protons across a membrane and use ATP synthase, but in chloroplasts protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen while in mitochondria they accumulate in the intermembrane space.
ref_029_03.subject: Biology

ref_029_04.text: Rubisco fixes CO₂ in the Calvin cycle but can also react with O₂ in photorespiration, wasting energy; C4 and CAM plants reduce this loss.
ref_029_04.subject: Biology

ref_029_05.text: Photosystem II splits water to release O₂ and feeds electrons through the chain to photosystem I, which reduces NADP⁺ to NADPH (the Z-scheme).
ref_029_05.subject: Biology

ref_029_06.text: The citric acid cycle oxidises acetyl-CoA to CO₂, generating NADH, FADH₂ and a small amount of GTP or ATP per turn in the mitochondrial matrix.
ref_029_06.subject: Biology

ref_029_07.text: Fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ without oxygen, yielding lactic acid or ethanol, but only 2 ATP per glucose.
ref_029_07.subject: Biology

ref_030_01.text: The definite integral is the limit of Riemann sums and equals the net signed area between the curve and the x-axis.
ref_030_01.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_02.text: The FTC part 2 states that ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a) where F' = f.
ref_030_02.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_03.text: The Taylor series of f about a is Σ f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)(x−a)ⁿ/n!, and its partial sums are polynomial approximations of f.
ref_030_03.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_04.text: Common integration techniques are substitution, integration by parts (∫u dv = uv − ∫v du) and partial fractions for rational functions.
ref_030_04.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_05.text: Improper integrals have infinite limits or unbounded integrands and are defined as limits; ∫₁^∞ 1/xᵖ dx converges only for p > 1.
ref_030_05.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_06.text: The Lagrange remainder bounds the error of a Taylor polynomial, and a power series converges within its radius of convergence, found via the ratio test.
ref_030_06.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_07.text: Maclaurin series: eˣ = Σ xⁿ/n!, sin x = Σ (−1)ⁿ x²ⁿ⁺¹/(2n+1)!, and 1/(1−x) = Σ xⁿ for |x| < 1.
ref_030_07.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_030_08.text: A differential equation relates a function to its derivatives; separable equations can be solved by integrating both sides after separating variables.
ref_030_08.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_031_01.text: Merge sort divides the array into two halves, conquers each recursively, and combines the results by merging.
ref_031_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_02.text: The recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) solves to O(n log n) by the master theorem: log n levels of recursion, each doing O(n) merging work.
ref_031_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_03.text: The merge step walks two pointers through the sorted halves, copying the smaller element each time, and needs O(n) auxiliary space for arrays.
ref_031_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_04.text: Merge sort is stable: when two elements compare equal, taking the left one first preserves their original relative order.
ref_031_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_05.text: Quicksort partitions around a pivot and averages O(n log n) but degrades to O(n²) with poor pivots; it sorts in place.
ref_031_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_06.text: Heapsort builds a max-heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum, achieving O(n log n) worst case in place but without stability.
ref_031_06.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_07.text: Timsort is a hybrid of merge sort and insertion sort that exploits existing runs; it is the default sort in Python and Java for objects.
ref_031_07.subject: Computer Science

ref_031_08.text: Counting sort sorts integers in a small range in O(n + k) time without comparisons.
ref_031_08.subject: Computer Science

ref_032_01.text: Doubling the distance between two masses reduces the gravitational force to one quarter.
ref_032_01.subject: Physics

ref_032_02.text: The gravitational field strength at distance r from mass M is g = GM/r²; at Earth's surface this gives about 9.8 m/s².
ref_032_02.subject: Physics

ref_032_03.text: For a circular orbit, gravity supplies the centripetal force, so orbital speed is v = √(GM/r), independent of the orbiting mass.
ref_032_03.subject: Physics

ref_032_04.text: Coulomb's law gives the electrostatic force F = k q₁q₂/r², also inverse-square, but it can be attractive or repulsive.
ref_032_04.subject: Physics

ref_032_05.text: Kepler's laws describe planetary orbits as ellipses with the Sun at one focus, equal areas swept in equal times, and T² proportional to a³.
ref_032_05.subject: Physics

ref_032_06.text: General relativity models gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy rather than as a force.
ref_032_06.subject: Physics

ref_032_07.text: Near a planet's surface, gravitational potential energy is U = mgh; for large distances U = −GMm/r.
ref_032_07.subject: Physics

ref_033_01.text: The principle predicts the direction of a shift but not its magnitude; magnitudes require the equilibrium constant expression.
ref_033_01.subject: Chemistry

ref_033_02.text: Adding reactant or removing product makes Q < K, so the reaction shifts forward; adding product makes Q > K, shifting it back.
ref_033_02.subject: Chemistry

ref_033_03.text: Increasing pressure (or decreasing volume) shifts a gaseous equilibrium toward the side with fewer moles of gas; if the moles are equal, there is no shift.
ref_033_03.subject: Chemistry

ref_033_04.text: Raising temperature favours the endothermic direction and lowering it favours the exothermic direction; unlike concentration or pressure changes, temperature changes alter the value of K.
ref_033_04.subject: Chemistry

ref_033_05.text: Reaction rate depends on concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts, and is described by the rate law rate = k[A]^m[B]^n.
ref_033_05.subject: Chemistry

ref_033_06.text: ΔG° = −RT ln K links standard free energy change to the equilibrium constant.
ref_033_06.subject: Chemistry

ref_034_01.text: Segregation is explained by meiosis: homologous chromosomes separate, so each gamete receives one allele of each gene.
ref_034_01.subject: Biology

ref_034_02.text: A recessive phenotype appears only in homozygous recessive individuals, because a dominant allele masks it in heterozygotes.
ref_034_02.subject: Biology

ref_034_03.text: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes (Aa × Aa) gives a 3:1 phenotype ratio and 1:2:1 genotype ratio in the F2 generation, which a Punnett square displays.
ref_034_03.subject: Biology

ref_034_04.text: The law of independent assortment says alleles of different genes segregate independently, giving a 9:3:3:1 ratio in dihybrid crosses of unlinked genes.
ref_034_04.subject: Biology

ref_034_05.text: Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries (homozygous or heterozygous), while phenotype is the observable trait that results.
ref_034_05.subject: Biology

ref_034_06.text: In incomplete dominance the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype, such as pink flowers from red × white parents.
ref_034_06.subject: Biology

ref_034_07.text: Sex-linked traits are carried on the X chromosome, so recessive X-linked conditions are more common in males, who have only one X.
ref_034_07.subject: Biology

ref_034_08.text: Epigenetic marks such as DNA methylation and histone modification alter gene expression without changing the DNA sequence.
ref_034_08.subject: Biology

ref_035_01.text: Big-O notation gives an asymptotic upper bound: f(n) = O(g(n)) means f grows no faster than a constant multiple of g for large n.
ref_035_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_035_02.text: Constant factors and lower-order terms are dropped, so 3n² + 5n + 2 is O(n²).
ref_035_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_035_03.text: Ω gives an asymptotic lower bound and Θ a tight bound, meaning both O and Ω hold.
ref_035_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_035_04.text: Space complexity measures the memory an algorithm uses as a function of input size, counting auxiliary space beyond the input.
ref_035_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_035_05.text: Amortized analysis averages the cost of a sequence of operations, showing that expensive operations are rare enough to keep the average cost low.
ref_035_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_036_01.text: The total linear momentum of an isolated system is constant, Σpᵢ = Σp_f, because internal forces are equal and opposite (Newton's third law).
ref_036_01.subject: Physics

ref_036_02.text: Linear momentum p = mv is a vector, so directions matter when adding momenta.
ref_036_02.subject: Physics

ref_036_03.text: In a perfectly inelastic collision the bodies move together afterwards, losing the maximum kinetic energy consistent with momentum conservation.
ref_036_03.subject: Physics

ref_036_04.text: Impulse is force multiplied by contact time and equals the change in momentum, J = FΔt = Δp.
ref_036_04.subject: Physics

ref_036_05.text: A rocket accelerates by expelling exhaust backwards, conserving momentum of the rocket–exhaust system.
ref_036_05.subject: Physics

ref_037_01.text: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
ref_037_01.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_037_02.text: The hypotenuse lies opposite the right angle and is always the longest side.
ref_037_02.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_037_03.text: The converse says a triangle whose sides satisfy a² + b² = c² must contain a right angle.
ref_037_03.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_037_04.text: The law of cosines, c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C, generalises the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle.
ref_037_04.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_037_05.text: Pythagorean triples such as (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13) are integer solutions to a² + b² = c².
ref_037_05.subject: Mathematics & Statistics

ref_038_01.text: LRU (least recently used) evicts the entry whose last access is oldest when capacity is exceeded.
ref_038_01.subject: Computer Science

ref_038_02.text: The standard LRU design pairs a hash table for O(1) lookup with a doubly linked list ordering entries by recency, giving O(1) get and put.
ref_038_02.subject: Computer Science

ref_038_03.text: Caches can serve stale data, so entries are given a time-to-live or invalidated on writes; write-through and write-back policies trade consistency for speed.
ref_038_03.subject: Computer Science

ref_038_04.text: LFU evicts the least frequently used entry, FIFO the oldest inserted; adaptive policies such as ARC balance recency and frequency.
ref_038_04.subject: Computer Science

ref_038_05.text: Modern CPUs have L1, L2 and L3 caches with increasing size and latency, and cache lines of typically 64 bytes.
ref_038_05.subject: Computer Science

ref_039_01.text: Light travels more slowly in materials than in vacuum, with speed v = c/n; the frequency stays constant while the wavelength shortens.
ref_039_01.subject: Physics

ref_039_02.text: Entering a medium with higher refractive index, light slows and bends toward the normal; entering a lower-index medium it bends away.
ref_039_02.subject: Physics

ref_039_03.text: The refractive index n = c/v compares the speed of light in vacuum with its speed in the medium; glass has n ≈ 1.5 and water n ≈ 1.33.
ref_039_03.subject: Physics

ref_039_04.text: Snell's law relates angles of incidence and refraction: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, where n = c/v is the refractive index.
ref_039_04.subject: Physics

ref_039_05.text: When light travels from a higher-index to a lower-index medium above the critical angle sin θc = n₂/n₁, it is totally reflected; optical fibres rely on this.
ref_039_05.subject: Physics

ref_039_06.text: Refractive index varies slightly with wavelength, so a prism separates white light into colours, since violet bends more than red.
ref_039_06.subject: Physics

ref_039_07.text: Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through an opening or around an obstacle, most noticeable when the size is comparable to the wavelength.
ref_039_07.subject: Physics

ref_040_01.text: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises.
ref_040_01.subject: Economics

ref_040_02.text: The law of supply states that quantity supplied rises with price, ceteris paribus.
ref_040_02.subject: Economics

ref_040_03.text: Equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, and the price there is the equilibrium price.
ref_040_03.subject: Economics

ref_040_04.text: A binding price ceiling below equilibrium causes shortages; a binding price floor above equilibrium causes surpluses.
ref_040_04.subject: Economics

ref_040_05.text: Price elasticity of demand measures how strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change; demand for necessities tends to be inelastic and for luxuries elastic.
ref_040_05.subject: Economics

ref_040_06.text: A monopolist sets marginal revenue equal to marginal cost and charges a price above marginal cost, creating deadweight loss.
ref_040_06.subject: Economics

g2_005.ref_005_03: Connections close with FIN and ACK exchanges in each direction; the side that closes first enters TIME_WAIT to absorb delayed segments.
g2_005.ref_005_04: The three-way handshake synchronises initial sequence numbers: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.
g2_005.ref_005_05: UDP is connectionless and offers no delivery, ordering or congestion guarantees, making it suitable for DNS and real-time media.

g2_007.ref_007_02: Batch gradient descent uses the full dataset per update; stochastic gradient descent uses one sample and mini-batch uses a small subset. Mini-batches balance noise, speed and hardware efficiency.

g2_008.ref_008_02: Threads sharing memory can suffer race conditions when unsynchronized accesses interleave. Mutexes, semaphores and atomic operations protect critical sections.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Binary search finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly comparing the target with the middle element and discarding half of the remaining range. It needs random access and a sorted input.
expected_relevant_facts: Binary search finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly comparing the target with the middle element and discarding half of the remaining range.
It needs random access and a sorted input.

concepts.note_evidence: sorted input

cases.reference_book_content: Each comparison halves the search range, so binary search takes O(log n) comparisons in the worst case. With n = 10^6 elements, at most about 20 comparisons are needed. Computing the midpoint as (lo + hi) / 2 can overflow fixed-width integers; lo + (hi - lo) / 2 avoids this. Loop invariants must be chosen carefully to avoid infinite loops and off-by-one errors. Binary search is only valid when the input is sorted by the comparison used in the search. On unsorted data the discard step can throw away the target. Interpolation search estimates the target position from key values and can reach O(log log n) on uniformly distributed data but degrades to O(n) on skewed data.

cases.subject: Physics
cases.input_note: Ohm's law says the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it: V = IR, where R is the resistance measured in ohms.
expected_relevant_facts: Ohm's law says the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it: V = IR, where R is the resistance measured in ohms.

concepts.note_evidence: resistance measured in ohms

cases.reference_book_content: Electrical power dissipated in a resistor is P = VI = I²R = V²/R. This energy appears as heat, known as Joule heating. Ohmic materials have a linear I–V curve with constant resistance. Diodes, filament bulbs and thermistors are non-ohmic: resistance changes with voltage or temperature. Resistance depends on geometry: R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length and A is cross-sectional area. Resistance is the opposition to current flow, measured in ohms (Ω), with 1 Ω = 1 V/A. Kirchhoff's current law states currents entering a junction sum to zero; the voltage law states voltage changes around any closed loop sum to zero.

cases.input_note: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery over an unreliable IP network. A connection is established with a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK). Lost segments are detected through acknowledgements and retransmitted.
expected_relevant_facts: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery over an unreliable IP network.
A connection is established with a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK).
Lost segments are detected through acknowledgements and retransmitted.

concepts.note_evidence: three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)

cases.reference_book_content: Flow control prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver. The receiver advertises a window size, and the sender limits unacknowledged data to that window. Congestion control adapts the sending rate to network capacity. Slow start grows the congestion window exponentially until a threshold, then additive increase/multiplicative decrease (AIMD) takes over. Connections close with FIN and ACK exchanges in each direction; the side that closes first enters TIME_WAIT to absorb delayed segments. The three-way handshake synchronises initial sequence numbers: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK. UDP is connectionless and offers no delivery, ordering or congestion guarantees, making it suitable for DNS and real-time media.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by repeatedly moving parameters in the direction of the negative gradient. The learning rate controls the step size.
expected_relevant_facts: Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by repeatedly moving parameters in the direction of the negative gradient.
The learning rate controls the step size.

concepts.note_evidence: The learning rate controls the step size
negative gradient

cases.reference_book_content: If the learning rate is too large, updates overshoot and the loss can diverge; if it is too small, convergence is very slow. Schedules such as step decay or cosine annealing reduce the rate over training. Batch gradient descent uses the full dataset per update; stochastic gradient descent uses one sample and mini-batch uses a small subset. Mini-batches balance noise, speed and hardware efficiency. Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying average of past gradients, which smooths oscillations across ravines and speeds progress along consistent directions. Adaptive methods such as Adagrad, RMSProp and Adam scale each parameter's step size using running statistics of its gradients. The gradient of the loss points toward steepest ascent, so parameters are updated by subtracting the gradient scaled by the learning rate. Newton's method uses second-order curvature (the Hessian) to take steps, converging quickly near a minimum but costing O(d²) memory and O(d³) time per step.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: A process is a running program with its own virtual address space. A thread is a unit of execution within a process; threads in the same process share the heap and global data but have separate stacks.
expected_relevant_facts: A process is a running program with its own virtual address space.
A thread is a unit of execution within a process; threads in the same process share the heap and global data but have separate stacks.

concepts.note_evidence: its own virtual address space
separate stacks

cases.reference_book_content: Switching between threads of the same process is cheaper than switching processes because the address space, and often TLB contents, need not change. Threads sharing memory can suffer race conditions when unsynchronized accesses interleave. Mutexes, semaphores and atomic operations protect critical sections. Separate processes communicate through IPC mechanisms such as pipes, sockets, message queues and shared memory, since they do not share address spaces by default. Each process has a private virtual address space, so one process cannot directly read or write another's memory. Each thread has its own stack and register state so it can run its own call chain independently. Green threads are scheduled by a language runtime rather than the OS kernel, allowing very cheap creation but complicating blocking system calls.

cases.subject: Mathematics & Statistics
cases.input_note: For a square matrix A, an eigenvector v is a nonzero vector such that Av = λv for a scalar λ, called the eigenvalue. Eigenvalues are found by solving det(A − λI) = 0.
expected_relevant_facts: For a square matrix A, an eigenvector v is a nonzero vector such that Av = λv for a scalar λ, called the eigenvalue.
Eigenvalues are found by solving det(A − λI) = 0.

concepts.note_evidence: det(A − λI) = 0

cases.reference_book_content: A matrix is diagonalizable if it has n linearly independent eigenvectors; then A = PDP⁻¹ with D diagonal, which makes computing powers of A easy. Algebraic multiplicity is the number of times λ appears as a root of the characteristic polynomial; geometric multiplicity is the dimension of its eigenspace, and it never exceeds the algebraic multiplicity. Real symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors, so they can be orthogonally diagonalized as A = QΛQᵀ. The characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) has degree n, so an n×n matrix has at most n distinct eigenvalues.

cases.reference_book_content: For launch speed v and angle θ on level ground, range R = v² sin(2θ)/g and maximum height H = v² sin²θ / (2g). Range is maximal at θ = 45°. cases.subject: Biology
cases.input_note: Natural selection favours heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction. Over generations, advantageous traits become more common in a population.
expected_relevant_facts: Natural selection favours heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction.
Over generations, advantageous traits become more common in a population.

concepts.note_evidence: heritable traits

cases.reference_book_content: Antibiotic use creates selection pressure: resistant bacteria survive and reproduce while susceptible ones die, so resistance alleles rapidly increase in frequency. Genetic drift is random change in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations. Founder effects and population bottlenecks are common causes. In evolutionary biology, fitness is relative reproductive success, not strength or health: the number of viable offspring an individual contributes to the next generation compared with others. Selection can only act on variation that is heritable; acquired traits that are not encoded in the genome are not passed on. Sexual selection favours traits that increase mating success, such as peacock tails, even when they reduce survival.

cases.input_note: The pH of a solution is −log₁₀[H⁺]. Strong acids dissociate completely in water, whereas weak acids only partially dissociate.
expected_relevant_facts: The pH of a solution is −log₁₀[H⁺].
Strong acids dissociate completely in water, whereas weak acids only partially dissociate.

concepts.note_evidence: weak acids only partially dissociate

aliases: negative log of hydrogen ion concentration
concepts.note_evidence: −log₁₀[H⁺]

cases.reference_book_content: The acid dissociation constant Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA] quantifies acid strength; pKa = −log Ka, and a smaller pKa means a stronger acid. A buffer contains a weak acid and its conjugate base and resists pH change. The Henderson–Hasselbalch equation gives pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]). In Brønsted–Lowry theory an acid donates a proton and forms its conjugate base; the stronger the acid, the weaker its conjugate base. Weak acids establish an equilibrium HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻ lying mostly to the left. A change of one pH unit corresponds to a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration. A titration curve plots pH against added titrant volume; the equivalence point is where moles of acid equal moles of base.

cases.reference_book_content: The core stack operations are push (add to top), pop (remove and return the top) and peek (read the top without removing it); all run in O(1) time. cases.reference_book_content: The page table is indexed by virtual page number and yields the physical frame number for that page. A page fault is handled by finding a free frame and reading the page from disk. The OS then updates the page table entry, whose dirty bit records whether the page must be written back on eviction. Besides LRU, common policies are FIFO, which can exhibit Belady's anomaly, and the clock algorithm, an inexpensive approximation of LRU using a reference bit. A two-level page table splits the virtual page number so that unused regions of the address space need no second-level tables, saving memory. The translation lookaside buffer (TLB) caches recent virtual-to-physical translations so most memory accesses avoid a page-table walk. A TLB miss triggers a page-table walk, and the TLB is typically flushed or tagged on context switch. Thrashing occurs when processes lack enough frames for their working sets, so the system spends most of its time servicing page faults rather than doing useful work. With demand paging pages are loaded only on first access. Copy-on-write lets fork share pages between parent and child until one writes, when the page is copied. cases.reference_book_content: Passive transport needs no cellular energy because it is driven by the concentration or electrochemical gradient. Active transport uses ATP or an ion gradient to move solutes against their gradient via pumps or coupled transporters. Channel proteins form gated pores for ions, while carrier proteins change shape to shuttle specific molecules such as glucose. The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in per ATP hydrolysed, maintaining the resting membrane potential and driving secondary transport. In a hypotonic solution cells gain water and may lyse; in a hypertonic solution they lose water and shrink (crenation, or plasmolysis in plant cells); isotonic solutions cause no net movement. Secondary active transport uses the gradient of one ion, established by primary pumps, to drive another molecule across the membrane, either in the same direction (symport) or the opposite (antiport). Large molecules and particles cross the membrane in vesicles: endocytosis (including phagocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis) brings material in, and exocytosis releases it. Membrane fluidity depends on temperature, fatty-acid saturation and cholesterol, which buffers fluidity: it restrains movement when warm and prevents tight packing when cold. Plant, fungal and bacterial cells have a rigid cell wall outside the plasma membrane that provides mechanical support.

cases.reference_book_content: A held-out test set gives an unbiased estimate of generalization only if it is never used for fitting or model selection. Accuracy is (TP + TN) divided by the total number of examples. An overfit model has low training error but high test error because it memorises idiosyncrasies of the training set. In k-fold cross-validation the data is divided into k folds; each fold is used once for validation while the remaining k − 1 train the model. Stratified folds preserve class proportions. Precision is TP/(TP+FP) and recall is TP/(TP+FN). The F1 score is their harmonic mean and is more informative than accuracy when classes are imbalanced. With 99% negatives, a classifier that always predicts negative scores 99% accuracy while detecting nothing, the accuracy paradox. Class weights and resampling help. The ROC curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate across thresholds; the area under it (AUC) measures ranking quality independent of any single threshold. Data leakage occurs when information from the test set influences training, for example by fitting a scaler on all the data before splitting, producing overly optimistic scores. The bias–variance tradeoff describes the tension between underfitting (high bias) and overfitting (high variance); expected error decomposes into bias², variance and irreducible noise. Reinforcement learning trains an agent to maximise cumulative reward through interaction with an environment.

cases.reference_book_content: Hooke's law F = −kx gives a linear restoring force, which is why springs produce SHM. In ideal SHM the period depends only on the mass and spring constant, not on how far the mass is displaced. The differential equation m x'' = −k x has sinusoidal solutions with amplitude A and phase φ set by initial conditions. For a simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g) for small angles, using sin θ ≈ θ; at larger amplitudes the period increases slightly. In SHM the total mechanical energy E = ½kA² is constant, oscillating between kinetic energy (maximal at equilibrium) and potential energy (maximal at the turning points). With damping, amplitude decays over time. Underdamped systems oscillate with shrinking amplitude, critically damped systems return fastest without oscillating, and overdamped systems return slowly. A periodically driven oscillator responds with maximum amplitude near its natural frequency, called resonance; damping limits and broadens the resonance peak. SHM is the projection of uniform circular motion onto a diameter: a point moving at angular speed ω around a circle of radius A has a projection that oscillates as A cos(ωt + φ). Superposed waves add: constructive interference occurs when crests align, destructive when a crest meets a trough.

cases.reference_book_content: In the array layout, the children of index i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2, so no pointers are needed. In a min-heap the smallest element is always at the root; siblings have no ordering constraint. Union-find (disjoint-set union) represents each set as a tree; find returns the root representative and union links two roots. In a trie each edge is labelled with a character and the path from the root spells a prefix, so words with common prefixes share nodes. Insert appends at the end and sifts up; extract-min swaps the root with the last element and sifts down. Both take O(log n), while building a heap from n elements with bottom-up heapify takes O(n). Heaps implement priority queues and power heapsort (O(n log n) time, in place), top-k selection, event simulation and Dijkstra's algorithm. Union by rank and path compression together make union-find operations run in amortized O(α(n)) time, where α is the inverse Ackermann function, effectively constant. Trie lookup, insert and prefix search take O(L) time for a key of length L regardless of the number of keys, but memory can be large; radix trees compress single-child chains. A segment tree answers range queries such as sum or minimum over an array in O(log n) and supports point updates.

cases.reference_book_content: The light reactions produce ATP and NADPH, which the Calvin cycle uses to fix CO₂ into G3P. Cellular respiration oxidises glucose in stages: glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Both organelles pump protons across a membrane and use ATP synthase, but in chloroplasts protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen while in mitochondria they accumulate in the intermembrane space. Rubisco fixes CO₂ in the Calvin cycle but can also react with O₂ in photorespiration, wasting energy; C4 and CAM plants reduce this loss. Photosystem II splits water to release O₂ and feeds electrons through the chain to photosystem I, which reduces NADP⁺ to NADPH (the Z-scheme). The citric acid cycle oxidises acetyl-CoA to CO₂, generating NADH, FADH₂ and a small amount of GTP or ATP per turn in the mitochondrial matrix. Fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ without oxygen, yielding lactic acid or ethanol, but only 2 ATP per glucose.

cases.reference_book_content: Merge sort divides the array into two halves, conquers each recursively, and combines the results by merging. The recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) solves to O(n log n) by the master theorem: log n levels of recursion, each doing O(n) merging work. The merge step walks two pointers through the sorted halves, copying the smaller element each time, and needs O(n) auxiliary space for arrays. Merge sort is stable: when two elements compare equal, taking the left one first preserves their original relative order. Quicksort partitions around a pivot and averages O(n log n) but degrades to O(n²) with poor pivots; it sorts in place. Heapsort builds a max-heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum, achieving O(n log n) worst case in place but without stability. Timsort is a hybrid of merge sort and insertion sort that exploits existing runs; it is the default sort in Python and Java for objects. Counting sort sorts integers in a small range in O(n + k) time without comparisons.

cases.input_note: Mendel's law of segregation says each individual carries two alleles for a trait and passes only one to each gamete. A dominant allele masks a recessive allele in heterozygotes.
expected_relevant_facts: Mendel's law of segregation says each individual carries two alleles for a trait and passes only one to each gamete.

cases.reference_book_content: Segregation is explained by meiosis: homologous chromosomes separate, so each gamete receives one allele of each gene. A recessive phenotype appears only in homozygous recessive individuals, because a dominant allele masks it in heterozygotes. A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes (Aa × Aa) gives a 3:1 phenotype ratio and 1:2:1 genotype ratio in the F2 generation, which a Punnett square displays. The law of independent assortment says alleles of different genes segregate independently, giving a 9:3:3:1 ratio in dihybrid crosses of unlinked genes. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries (homozygous or heterozygous), while phenotype is the observable trait that results. In incomplete dominance the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype, such as pink flowers from red × white parents. Sex-linked traits are carried on the X chromosome, so recessive X-linked conditions are more common in males, who have only one X. Epigenetic marks such as DNA methylation and histone modification alter gene expression without changing the DNA sequence.

cases.reference_book_content: Big-O notation gives an asymptotic upper bound: f(n) = O(g(n)) means f grows no faster than a constant multiple of g for large n. Constant factors and lower-order terms are dropped, so 3n² + 5n + 2 is O(n²). Ω gives an asymptotic lower bound and Θ a tight bound, meaning both O and Ω hold. Space complexity measures the memory an algorithm uses as a function of input size, counting auxiliary space beyond the input. Amortized analysis averages the cost of a sequence of operations, showing that expensive operations are rare enough to keep the average cost low.

cases.reference_book_content: The total linear momentum of an isolated system is constant, Σpᵢ = Σp_f, because internal forces are equal and opposite (Newton's third law). Linear momentum p = mv is a vector, so directions matter when adding momenta. In a perfectly inelastic collision the bodies move together afterwards, losing the maximum kinetic energy consistent with momentum conservation. Impulse is force multiplied by contact time and equals the change in momentum, J = FΔt = Δp. A rocket accelerates by expelling exhaust backwards, conserving momentum of the rocket–exhaust system.

cases.reference_book_content: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse lies opposite the right angle and is always the longest side. The converse says a triangle whose sides satisfy a² + b² = c² must contain a right angle. The law of cosines, c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C, generalises the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle. Pythagorean triples such as (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13) are integer solutions to a² + b² = c².

cases.input_note: An LRU cache keeps the most recently used items and throws away the item that has gone unused the longest when it is full. It is usually built from a hash map for constant-time lookup plus a doubly linked list that tracks recency, so both get and put run in constant time.
expected_relevant_facts: An LRU cache keeps the most recently used items and throws away the item that has gone unused the longest when it is full.

cases.reference_book_content: LRU (least recently used) evicts the entry whose last access is oldest when capacity is exceeded. The standard LRU design pairs a hash table for O(1) lookup with a doubly linked list ordering entries by recency, giving O(1) get and put. Caches can serve stale data, so entries are given a time-to-live or invalidated on writes; write-through and write-back policies trade consistency for speed. LFU evicts the least frequently used entry, FIFO the oldest inserted; adaptive policies such as ARC balance recency and frequency. Modern CPUs have L1, L2 and L3 caches with increasing size and latency, and cache lines of typically 64 bytes.

cases.input_note: When light passes from one transparent medium into another, it changes speed and bends at the boundary. Light moving into a slower medium such as glass bends toward the normal. The amount of bending depends on how much the speeds differ.
expected_relevant_facts: When light passes from one transparent medium into another, it changes speed and bends at the boundary.
Light moving into a slower medium such as glass bends toward the normal.
The amount of bending depends on how much the speeds differ.

cases.reference_book_content: Light travels more slowly in materials than in vacuum, with speed v = c/n; the frequency stays constant while the wavelength shortens. Entering a medium with higher refractive index, light slows and bends toward the normal; entering a lower-index medium it bends away. The refractive index n = c/v compares the speed of light in vacuum with its speed in the medium; glass has n ≈ 1.5 and water n ≈ 1.33. Snell's law relates angles of incidence and refraction: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, where n = c/v is the refractive index. When light travels from a higher-index to a lower-index medium above the critical angle sin θc = n₂/n₁, it is totally reflected; optical fibres rely on this. Refractive index varies slightly with wavelength, so a prism separates white light into colours, since violet bends more than red. Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through an opening or around an obstacle, most noticeable when the size is comparable to the wavelength.

cases.reference_book_content: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises. The law of supply states that quantity supplied rises with price, ceteris paribus. Equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, and the price there is the equilibrium price. A binding price ceiling below equilibrium causes shortages; a binding price floor above equilibrium causes surpluses. Price elasticity of demand measures how strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change; demand for necessities tends to be inelastic and for luxuries elastic. A monopolist sets marginal revenue equal to marginal cost and charges a price above marginal cost, creating deadweight loss.
